name: O'Neill
band_note: core tee $29 and core blouse $58 (women's price pass, 2026-10-13)
why: Surf-styled women's swimwear, dresses, knits and boardshorts mostly $40–$90, sold through its own outlet stores and US site, Nordstrom and surf shops; wetsuits sold on its EU site.
origin: Founded in San Francisco, United States in 1952 by Jack O'Neill.

onething.p: Women Hyperfreak Plus 4/3mm Chest Zip Full Wetsuit

ownership.owner: Surf & Turf / O'Neill Trademark (brand owner); US apparel licensed to La Jolla Sport U.S.A., Inc. (La Jolla Group) through Fall/Holiday 2027

quote.q: We are here to enable and inspire you to enjoy your playground longer.

opview: “We are here to enable and inspire you to enjoy your playground longer.” — O'Neill (house), About Us, eu.oneill.com

facts_read.source: brand site (US and EU); us.oneill.com terms; eu.oneill.com terms; Shop Eat Surf Outdoor 2026-07-29 and 2026-09-30; nordstrom.com search; hansensurf.com search; Vinted catalogue; TRR designer directory; B Lab directory; GOTS database

price_read.sublines: O'Neill women's clothing (product type WOMENS, incl. O'Riginals and TRVLR); EXCLUDED: swimwear, wetsuits, snow, men's, girls/boys, bags

doors.note: Stores page 'O'Neill Stores' carousel lists 12, all at outlet-centre addresses (classified outlet by address; pages do not name the centre). Storemapper dealer feed adds 5 more O'Neill outlets (Ontario Mills, Orange, Palm Beach, Sawgrass Mills, Tampa/Lutz) and 3 'O'Neill Surf Shop' doors in Santa Cruz/Capitola (counted own-door; operator flagged). Remaining ~1320 Storemapper rows are dealers/wholesale. No full-price O'Neill-branded mall store other than the Surf Shops.

fibre.sample: stratified sample of 80 across 13 derived categories, proportional; 331 styles from womens-clothing (599 listings) + womens-snow-jackets + womens-snow-pants fee

tech_evidence.names: HyperDry (water-repellent treatment, O'Neill's own); PrimaLoft insulation (licensed); FWC snow line with 20K/20K membrane and 'V-Design Body Mapping'
tech_evidence.owned: both — HyperDry and V-Design own names; PrimaLoft licensed
tech_evidence.share: 4% (14 of 331 styles name FWC, TRVLR+HyperDry or PrimaLoft)

craft_evidence.mills: no (REPREVE recycled-polyester yarn named on 9 styles, which is a fibre brand, not a mill)
craft_evidence.madein: 0% (no country of make in the feed or on the sampled PDPs)
craft_evidence.heritage: dated and placed — first surf shop 1952, Great Highway, San Francisco; moved to Santa Cruz in the 1960s (about the wetsuit business, not women's clothing)
craft_evidence.process: no for clothing — specs give fabric weight (GSM) and yarn singles, not how garments are made
craft_evidence.reasoning: The women's clothing pages state fabric and weight but never where or by whom it is made, so nothing about making can be checked. The dated San Francisco and Santa Cruz heritage is about wetsuits and does not cover this range.
